scenario: 面试要你「设计语义搜索」（Google/Amazon/LinkedIn 搜索）——语义搜索 = 按向量相似度而非字面关键词找结果。
scenario_en: You are asked to design semantic search (Google/Amazon/LinkedIn), where results are found by vector similarity rather than literal keywords.
q: 语义搜索题，面试官首先在考什么？
q_en: In a semantic-search question, what is the interviewer testing first?
why: 搜索是 MAANG 最高频的 ML 系统设计题，考点是「先 framing 再解题」——先讲清查询理解、业务指标、规模约束三根支柱，再落到 query encoder→ANN→re-ranker→SERP 这条主线。上来就堆模型、跳过 framing 是最典型的失分点。
why_en: Search is the most-asked ML system-design topic, and the test is whether you frame before you solve, laying out query understanding, business metrics, and scale constraints before drawing the encoder-to-ANN-to-ranker pipeline.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["查询 query"] --> E["query encoder
编码成向量"] E --> A["ANN 索引
近似最近邻召回"] A --> R["re-ranker
精排"] R --> S["SERP
结果页"]
options: 上来就选最强的排序模型，把召回和延迟当实现细节，先把准确率堆到最高
先背出 HNSW 的图结构底层细节，证明你懂 ANN 原理，再谈别的
先做 framing：讲清查询理解、业务指标、规模约束三支柱，再落到 encoder→ANN→re-ranker 主线
先问清前端用什么框架、SERP 页面怎么渲染，把交互设计先定下来
options_en: Jump straight to the strongest ranking model, treating recall and latency as implementation details, and max out accuracy first.
Recite HNSW's graph internals first to prove you understand ANN, then discuss the rest.
Frame first — query understanding, business metrics, scale constraints — then draw the encoder-to-ANN-to-ranker pipeline.
Ask which frontend framework and how the SERP renders, and pin down the interaction design first.
optionExplanations: 直接堆模型跳过 framing 正是失分点，你没说清优化什么指标、扛多大规模，模型再强也接不住追问。
HNSW 底层是加分细节不是开场；不先 framing 就钻实现，面试官会觉得你没有系统思路。
对；framing 三支柱 + 主线管道是 L4 起步就该给的骨架，之后每个深挖都挂在它上面。
前端框架不是 ML 系统设计考点；语义搜索的难点在检索质量、延迟和规模，不在页面渲染。
optionExplanations_en: Piling on models while skipping framing is the classic miss — without a target metric or scale, even a strong model cannot survive follow-ups.
HNSW internals are a bonus, not the opener; diving into implementation before framing signals no systems thinking.
Correct — the three pillars plus the pipeline are the skeleton expected from L4 up, and every deep-dive hangs off it.
Frontend frameworks are not the ML-design test; the hard parts are retrieval quality, latency, and scale, not rendering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指头部科技公司群，这里代表最常出这类系统设计题的雇主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAANG (Meta, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Google) refers to top tech employers that most often ask these system-design questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻：牺牲少量召回换取在超大向量库上的亚秒检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) trades a little recall for sub-second retrieval over a huge vector index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索结果页：把召回并排好序的结果组装展示给用户的那一页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SERP (Search Engine Results Page) is the assembled, ranked page of results shown to the user.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按含义（向量相似度）而非字面关键词匹配来检索结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Semantic search retrieves by meaning (vector similarity) rather than literal keyword match.

scenario: 语义搜索的工业标准架构是「稠密向量嵌入 + ANN」，而不是传统关键词倒排（如 BM25）。
scenario_en: The industry-standard architecture for semantic search is dense vector embeddings plus ANN, not classic keyword inverted indexes like BM25.
q: 稠密向量检索比关键词匹配强在哪一维？
q_en: On what dimension do dense embeddings beat keyword matching?
why: 稠密向量把查询和文档映射到同一语义空间、按相似度召回，能命中「换个说法」的查询；BM25 这类关键词只按字面词频匹配，遇到同义词就漏召回。代价是向量要额外的 ANN 索引，也不如关键词可解释。
why_en: Dense embeddings map query and doc into one semantic space and retrieve by similarity, catching synonyms and rewordings that keyword BM25 misses on literal terms.
tradeoff: 稠密向量（懂语义、召回同义/近义）vs 关键词 BM25（只匹字面词、快且可解释）
options: 稠密向量按语义相似度召回，能命中同义词与换一种说法的查询
稠密向量天生比倒排索引快，所以选它纯粹是为了更低的检索延迟
稠密向量不用任何索引，直接全库暴力算相似度也能毫秒返回
关键词匹配召回一定更全，向量只是用来给结果做最后的美化重排
options_en: Dense vectors retrieve by semantic similarity, catching synonyms and reworded queries.
Dense vectors are inherently faster than inverted indexes, so you pick them purely for lower latency.
Dense vectors need no index — brute-forcing similarity over the whole corpus still returns in milliseconds.
Keyword matching always recalls more, and vectors only prettify the final re-rank.
optionExplanations: 对；同一语义空间里「laptop」和「notebook computer」离得近，向量能召回，BM25 字面不同就漏。
快慢取决于索引结构不是向量本身；十亿级暴力算向量反而比倒排慢，所以才要上 ANN。
不用索引就得全库线性扫描，十亿向量根本做不到毫秒级，这正是要上 ANN 的原因。
关键词召回不是更全，它对换词表达系统性漏召回；向量正是来补这块语义召回的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — in one semantic space 'laptop' sits near 'notebook computer', so vectors recall it while BM25 misses the differing literal.
Speed depends on the index structure, not the vector itself; brute-force vector scan at billion scale is slower than an inverted index, hence ANN.
No index means a full linear scan, impossible in milliseconds at billion scale — exactly why ANN exists.
Keyword recall is not broader; it systematically misses rewordings, which is the semantic gap vectors fill.

termDefinitions.term: dense vector embedding / 稠密向量嵌入
termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本编码成一个低维稠密向量，语义相近的文本向量距离近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dense vector embedding encodes text into a low-dimensional dense vector where semantically similar texts sit close.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典关键词检索打分函数，按词频/逆文档频率匹配字面词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Best Match 25) is a classic keyword-ranking function scoring literal term overlap via term and inverse-document frequency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索，牺牲少量召回换取大规模亚秒检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) trades a little recall for sub-second retrieval at scale.

q: 补全语义搜索 framing 的三根支柱：
q_en: Fill in the three pillars of semantic-search framing.
text: 无论 Google、Amazon 还是 LinkedIn 搜索，framing 都围绕三根支柱：{{查询理解}}、{{业务指标}}、{{规模约束}}。
text_en: For Google, Amazon, or LinkedIn search, framing rests on three pillars: {{query understanding}}, {{business metrics}}, and {{scale constraints}}.
why: 这三根支柱是任何搜索题的开场骨架：查询理解决定召回上限，业务指标定义「做得好」，规模约束决定架构选型。缺任何一根，后面的深挖都没有落点。
why_en: The three pillars — query understanding, business metrics, and scale constraints — are the opening skeleton every search deep-dive hangs off.

scenario: 用户查询「apple」——不知道指水果、公司还是别的，检索质量的天花板就卡在这里。
scenario_en: A user queries 'apple' — unclear if it means the fruit, the company, or something else, and retrieval quality caps out here.
q: 为什么说查询理解是检索质量的上游瓶颈？
q_en: Why is query understanding the upstream bottleneck on retrieval quality?
why: 检索质量被查询理解封顶——「apple」不带上下文就无从判断意图，召回再强也可能整批跑偏。查询理解是独立的上游 ML 问题，它的输出喂给下游的检索和排序。
why_en: Retrieval is capped by query understanding — 'apple' with no context gives no intent, so even strong recall can be entirely wrong, since understanding is the upstream ML problem feeding retrieval and ranking.
options: 查询理解只是转小写、去停用词的文本预处理，属于工程清洗，不算 ML 问题
查询越长模型越准，所以查询理解的目标是想办法让用户多打字、把查询写长
查询理解只影响结果页排得好不好看，不改变到底召回哪一批候选文档
意图不清（如「apple」）会让召回从源头跑偏，它是喂给下游检索排序的上游 ML 问题
options_en: Query understanding is just lowercasing and stopword removal — a cleaning step, not an ML problem.
Longer queries are more accurate, so query understanding aims to make users type more.
Query understanding only affects how nicely the page ranks, not which candidates get recalled.
Unclear intent (like 'apple') skews recall at the source; it is the upstream ML problem feeding retrieval and ranking.
optionExplanations: 转小写去停用词只是最表层；意图分类、实体识别、消歧都是要建模的 ML 任务，不是清洗。
真实查询平均才约 3 词，逼用户多打字不现实；系统要在短查询下猜准意图，不是求长。
意图错了召回的候选就整批错，不只是排序问题；理解决定的是候选池本身。
对；「apple」没上下文就无法判断意图，召回从源头偏，所以理解是检索质量的天花板。
optionExplanations_en: Lowercasing and stopwords are the surface; intent classification, entity recognition, and disambiguation are modeled ML tasks, not cleaning.
Real queries average ~3 words; forcing more typing is unrealistic — the system must infer intent from short queries.
Wrong intent means the whole candidate set is wrong, not just ranking; understanding decides the candidate pool itself.
Correct — 'apple' with no context has no inferable intent, so recall skews at the source, capping retrieval quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把原始查询解析成意图、实体、消歧后的结构，喂给下游检索排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query understanding parses a raw query into intent, entities, and disambiguated meaning that feed retrieval and ranking.

scenario: 查询理解要拆成可建模的子问题，各用一个模型（或共享多任务模型）解决。
scenario_en: Query understanding decomposes into modelable sub-problems, each solved by a model (or a shared multi-task model).
q: 查询理解包含哪些子问题？(多选)
q_en: Which are sub-problems of query understanding? (multiple)
why: 查询理解拆成意图分类、实体识别、上下文消歧三个子任务，各自输出喂给检索+排序；索引的存储结构是检索层的实现，不属于查询理解。
why_en: Query understanding splits into intent classification, entity recognition, and contextual disambiguation, whose outputs feed retrieval and ranking, while index storage is a retrieval-layer concern.
options: 意图分类：判断查询是导航型 / 信息型 / 交易型
实体识别：从查询里抽出角色 / 公司 / 地点 / 品牌等结构化实体
上下文消歧：靠会话和历史解决一词多义（Apple 公司 vs 水果）
把索引从倒排改成 B 树，降低磁盘寻道次数
options_en: Intent classification: is the query navigational, informational, or transactional.
Entity recognition: extract structured entities like role, company, location, brand.
Contextual disambiguation: resolve polysemy via session and history (Apple company vs fruit).
Switch the index from inverted to a B-tree to cut disk seeks.
optionExplanations: 对；意图型别决定用哪个索引和排序模型，是查询理解的第一层。
对；抽出的结构化实体变成过滤条件，在稠密召回前先缩小候选池。
对；一词多义靠会话上下文和用户历史消歧，否则「Apple」召回全乱。
错；倒排改 B 树是检索层的存储实现，和「理解查询意思」无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the intent type selects which index and ranking model to use, the first layer of understanding.
Correct — extracted structured entities become filters that shrink the candidate pool before dense recall.
Correct — polysemy is resolved by session context and user history, or 'Apple' recall goes haywire.
Incorrect — inverted-to-B-tree is a retrieval-layer storage choice, unrelated to understanding the query's meaning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文本分类，把查询分到导航/信息/交易等意图类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Intent classification is text classification sorting a query into navigational, informational, or transactional intent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 命名实体识别：从查询里抽出角色、公司、地点、品牌等结构化实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entity recognition (NER, Named Entity Recognition) extracts structured entities like role, company, location, or brand from a query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用会话上下文和用户历史解决一词多义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contextual disambiguation resolves polysemy using session context and user history.

scenario: 用户搜「LinkedIn login」——这是导航型查询，用户明确知道要去哪个页面。
scenario_en: A user searches 'LinkedIn login' — a navigational query where the user already knows the exact destination.
q: 识别出导航型意图后，检索管道该怎么变？
q_en: Once navigational intent is detected, how should the retrieval pipeline change?
why: 意图分类（文本分类到导航/信息/交易三类）决定用哪个索引和排序模型；导航型意图目标唯一，可以跳过完整精排、直接返回那个确定结果，省下排序延迟。
why_en: Intent classification picks the index and ranking model, and a navigational query has a single target, so you can skip full re-ranking and return the known result directly to save latency.
tradeoff: 导航型跳过精排（目标唯一、省延迟）vs 信息/交易型走完整精排（候选多、要比较）
whenOtherWins: 如果是信息型或交易型查询（如「best noise-cancelling headphones」），候选多、需要比较排序，就必须走完整召回+精排，不能跳。
options: 无论什么意图都走完整召回+精排，导航型也照跑一遍，保证一致
导航型目标唯一，可跳过完整精排直接返回确定结果，省下排序延迟
导航型反而要叠更多排序模型，因为这类用户的要求最高
把导航型查询直接丢弃不处理，让用户自己去点浏览器书签
options_en: Run full recall plus re-ranking for every intent — navigational too — to stay consistent.
A navigational query has one target, so skip full re-ranking and return the known result, saving latency.
Navigational queries need extra ranking models because those users demand the most.
Just drop navigational queries and let users click their own browser bookmark.
optionExplanations: 导航型目标唯一还跑完整精排是白费延迟；意图分类的价值就是按类型走不同路径。
对；「LinkedIn login」只有一个正确落点，跳过精排直接命中，省下 30–60ms 排序开销。
目标唯一的查询不需要更重的排序；加模型只增延迟不增质量，方向反了。
丢弃查询等于放弃这次搜索，导航型恰恰最容易满足，应快速命中而非放弃。
optionExplanations_en: Full re-ranking a single-target query wastes latency; the point of intent classification is to route by type.
Correct — 'LinkedIn login' has one right destination, so skipping re-rank hits it directly and saves the 30-60ms ranking budget.
A single-target query needs no heavier ranking; adding models only adds latency, not quality — backwards.
Dropping the query abandons the search; navigational is the easiest to satisfy and should hit fast, not be discarded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 三类查询意图：找特定页、查信息、完成交易；类型决定走哪条检索路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Navigational, informational, and transactional are three query intents — reach a page, learn something, complete a purchase — that route retrieval differently.

scenario: LinkedIn 搜「senior ML engineer at Meta in NYC」——里面有角色、公司、地点三个结构化实体。
scenario_en: On LinkedIn, 'senior ML engineer at Meta in NYC' contains three structured entities: role, company, location.
q: 抽出这些实体后，最该拿它们做什么？
q_en: Once these entities are extracted, what should you do with them?
why: 实体识别（NER）把查询里的角色/公司/地点抽成结构化字段，变成过滤条件，在稠密向量召回前先把候选缩小，既提精度又省下游算力。
why_en: NER turns role/company/location into structured filters that narrow the candidate pool before dense retrieval, raising precision and saving downstream compute.
tradeoff: 结构化实体先过滤（缩小候选、提精度）vs 纯稠密召回（无结构时唯一选择）
whenOtherWins: 如果查询是纯自然语言、没有可抽的结构化实体（如「how do neural nets learn」），就只能靠稠密语义召回，实体过滤帮不上。
options: 把实体拼回一个更长的字符串，喂给同一个向量编码器，别的不变
用实体去扩展查询词，让查询变长以匹配更多文档
忽略实体，直接把原始查询做稠密召回，实体只留着做日志分析
把实体变成结构化过滤条件，在稠密召回前先缩小候选池
options_en: Concatenate the entities back into a longer string and feed the same encoder, changing nothing else.
Use the entities to expand query terms so the query grows and matches more documents.
Ignore the entities, do dense recall on the raw query, and keep entities only for log analysis.
Turn the entities into structured filters that narrow the candidate pool before dense recall.
optionExplanations: 拼成长字符串再编码丢掉了结构；实体的价值是当过滤器，不是把查询拉长。
扩展查询词会引入噪声、放大候选；结构化实体应做精确过滤而非模糊扩召。
只拿实体做日志浪费了它；抽出的实体应直接进检索路径当过滤器缩小候选。
对；role=ML engineer、company=Meta、location=NYC 变成过滤，先砍候选再做向量召回。
optionExplanations_en: Concatenating into a long string discards structure; the entity's value is as a filter, not padding the query.
Expanding terms injects noise and inflates candidates; structured entities should filter precisely, not fuzzily expand.
Using entities only for logs wastes them; extracted entities should enter retrieval as filters to shrink candidates.
Correct — role=ML engineer, company=Meta, location=NYC become filters that cut candidates before vector recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从查询抽出结构化实体（角色/公司/地点/品牌）用作过滤条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Entity recognition (NER, Named Entity Recognition) extracts structured entities (role/company/location/brand) to use as filters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用抽出的字段（如 company=Meta）在召回前先精确缩小候选集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A structured filter uses extracted fields (e.g. company=Meta) to exactly narrow the candidate set before recall.

scenario: 用户搜「Java developer」——可能指编程语言 Java，也可能指印尼爪哇岛；「Apple」可能是公司或水果。
scenario_en: 'Java developer' could mean the language or the island of Java; 'Apple' could mean the company or the fruit.
q: 一词多义（polysemy）该靠什么来消歧？
q_en: What should resolve polysemy (one word, many meanings)?
why: 上下文消歧靠会话上下文和用户历史解决一词多义——同一个「Apple」在浏览科技新闻的用户和查食谱的用户那里指向不同。脱离上下文，词本身给不出答案。
why_en: Contextual disambiguation resolves polysemy via session context and user history — the same 'Apple' means different things to a tech-news reader and a recipe searcher — since the word alone gives no answer.
tradeoff: 会话/历史消歧（有上下文时准）vs 词典先验（冷启动无上下文时兜底）
whenOtherWins: 如果是全新用户、没有会话或历史信号（冷启动），只能靠词典先验或返回多义混合结果，让用户点选来澄清。
options: 靠会话上下文和用户历史：查科技的人搜 Apple 指公司
靠把查询转成小写并去掉标点，标准化后歧义自然消失
靠返回所有可能含义的结果，让用户翻十页自己找到对的
靠给查询定一个固定默认含义，永远当成最常见那个意思处理
options_en: Session context and user history: a tech reader searching Apple means the company.
Lowercasing and stripping punctuation so ambiguity disappears after normalization.
Returning results for every possible meaning and letting users page through to find the right one.
Assigning a fixed default meaning, always treating it as the most common sense.
optionExplanations: 对；同一个「Apple」，看科技新闻的用户指公司、查食谱的指水果，上下文才能分开。
大小写和标点标准化解决不了语义歧义；「Apple」大小写一样，意思还是两个。
全量返回把消歧推给用户，体验差；系统该用上下文先猜准再返回。
固定默认含义会系统性伤害少数意图用户，且忽略了会话里现成的消歧信号。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the same 'Apple' means company to a tech-news reader and fruit to a recipe searcher; only context separates them.
Case and punctuation normalization cannot fix semantic ambiguity; 'Apple' has one casing but two meanings.
Returning everything pushes disambiguation onto the user; the system should infer from context first.
A fixed default systematically hurts minority-intent users and ignores the disambiguation signal already in the session.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个词有多个意思（Apple=公司/水果），需靠上下文选出正确含义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polysemy is one word carrying multiple meanings (Apple = company or fruit), needing context to pick the right sense.

scenario: 查询理解的三个子问题（意图、实体、消歧）要落地成模型。
scenario_en: Query understanding's three sub-problems (intent, entity, disambiguation) must be realized as models.
q: 这些子问题在工程上怎么组织成模型？
q_en: How are these sub-problems organized into models in practice?
why: 三个子问题既可各用一个独立模型，也可合成一个共享的多任务模型；无论哪种，它们的输出都往下游喂给检索和排序。这是工程取舍，不是非此即彼的对错。
why_en: The sub-problems can each be a separate model or fold into one shared multi-task model, and either way their outputs feed downstream retrieval and ranking — an engineering tradeoff, not a right/wrong choice.
options: 必须三个子问题合成一个大模型，分开做一定更慢更差
必须各用一个完全独立的模型，共享参数会互相污染
可用独立模型分别做，也可合成共享多任务模型，输出都喂下游检索排序
这三个子问题应该放到排序阶段之后再做，属于结果后处理
options_en: You must fold all three into one big model — separate models are always slower and worse.
You must use fully separate models — sharing parameters would cross-contaminate them.
Use separate models or a shared multi-task model; either way, outputs feed downstream retrieval and ranking.
These sub-problems belong after ranking, as post-processing of results.
optionExplanations: 合成一个不是硬性要求；独立模型便于单独迭代，多任务省算力，各有取舍。
独立也不是唯一解；共享多任务模型常能借任务间相关性提升样本效率。
对；分开或多任务都行，是工程取舍；关键是输出统一喂给检索+排序。
查询理解是上游，必须在召回前完成；放到排序后就来不及指导召回了。
optionExplanations_en: Folding into one is not mandatory; separate models ease independent iteration while multi-task saves compute — a tradeoff.
Separate is not the only way; a shared multi-task model often gains sample efficiency from task correlation.
Correct — separate or multi-task both work as an engineering tradeoff; the key is outputs feeding retrieval and ranking.
Query understanding is upstream and must finish before recall; placing it after ranking is too late to guide recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个模型同时学多个相关任务（意图+实体+消歧），共享表示、省算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multi-task model learns several related tasks (intent, entity, disambiguation) at once, sharing representations to save compute.

scenario: 搜索查询平均约 3 个 token，目标文档却有几千 token——查询短、文档长。
scenario_en: A search query averages ~3 tokens but the target document spans thousands — short query, long document.
q: 查询-文档长度不匹配为什么会伤检索质量？
q_en: Why does query-document length mismatch hurt retrieval quality?
why: 查询只有约 3 词、携带的信号稀疏，和几千词的文档放同一空间比相似度时，短查询这端信息量太少、语义表达不足，召回容易偏。Staff+ 面试官专爱追这个点。
why_en: A ~3-word query carries sparse signal, so comparing it to a thousand-word document in one space leaves the short side under-expressed and skews recall, which Staff+ interviewers probe.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["查询 ~3 token
信号稀疏"] --> C{"同一语义空间
比相似度"} D["文档 ~数千 token
信号密集"] --> C C --> R["短查询端表达不足
召回易偏"]
options: 因为长文档一定包含查询所有词，匹配太容易，反而召回太多噪声
查询约 3 词信号稀疏，和几千词文档比相似度时短查询端表达不足、召回易偏
因为 token 数不同会让两端向量维度不同，无法计算余弦相似度
因为长文档编码更慢，纯粹是延迟问题，和召回质量本身无关
options_en: Because a long doc always contains all query terms, matching is too easy and recalls too much noise.
A ~3-word query is sparse, so vs a thousand-word doc the short side is under-expressed and recall skews.
Because differing token counts make the two vectors different dimensions, so cosine similarity cannot be computed.
Because long docs encode slower — purely a latency issue, unrelated to recall quality itself.
optionExplanations: 长文档不必含查询所有词（语义召回本就不靠字面）；问题是短查询信号太少，不是太多。
对；3 词 vs 几千词，短查询携带的语义信号稀疏，同一空间比相似度时这端吃亏，召回偏。
向量维度由编码器固定，和输入 token 数无关；余弦相似度照常能算，这不是问题所在。
长文档慢是延迟话题；这里的痛点是短查询信号稀疏导致的召回质量下降，不是速度。
optionExplanations_en: A long doc need not contain every query term (semantic recall is not literal); the issue is too little query signal, not too much.
Correct — 3 words vs thousands leaves the query semantically sparse, so it loses out in the shared space and recall skews.
Vector dimension is fixed by the encoder, not by input token count; cosine still computes, so that is not the issue.
Slow long-doc encoding is a latency topic; the pain here is recall degradation from sparse query signal, not speed.

termDefinitions.term: query-document length mismatch / 查询-文档长度不匹配
termDefinitions.meaning: 查询几词、文档几千词，短查询信号稀疏，同空间比相似度时召回偏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query-document length mismatch: a few-word query vs a thousand-word doc leaves the query sparse, skewing similarity recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文本被切成的最小单位（词或子词），是编码器的输入粒度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the smallest unit text is split into (word or subword), the encoder's input granularity.

scenario: 你要缓解查询-文档长度不匹配：文档几千 token、查询几词，直接整篇编码召回不稳。
scenario_en: You must mitigate query-document length mismatch: docs are thousands of tokens, queries a few words, and whole-doc encoding retrieves unstably.
q: 有哪两类主流缓解手段？
q_en: What are the two mainstream mitigations?
why: 两条路：passage-level indexing 把长文档切成段落分别编码入库，让查询匹配到最相关那一段；asymmetric encoder 用两个不同编码器分别处理短查询和长文档，各自适配长度。二者都在补短查询和长文档的表达鸿沟。
why_en: Two paths: passage-level indexing splits long docs into separately-indexed passages so the query matches the most relevant one, and an asymmetric encoder uses different encoders for short queries and long docs to fit each length.
tradeoff: passage-level indexing（切段、索引变大但定位精准）vs asymmetric encoder（双编码器、结构复杂但天然适配长度差）
whenOtherWins: 如果文档本身就短（如商品标题、人名），长度差不大，不切段也不用非对称编码器，直接对称编码就够。
options: passage-level indexing 切段分别索引，或 asymmetric encoder 用双编码器分别处理查询和文档
把查询强行补到几千 token，让它和文档一样长再一起编码
只索引每篇文档的前 100 个 token，其余部分截断丢弃掉
调大 ANN 的召回数量，多召回一些候选来掩盖这种不匹配
options_en: Passage-level indexing splits docs into separately indexed passages, or an asymmetric encoder handles query and doc with two encoders.
Pad the query to thousands of tokens so it is as long as the document, then co-encode.
Index only each doc's first 100 tokens and truncate away the rest.
Raise ANN's recall count to pull more candidates and mask the mismatch.
optionExplanations: 对；切段让查询命中最相关段落，双编码器让长短两端各用适配的编码器，都在补表达鸿沟。
把 3 词查询硬撑到几千 token 会灌进噪声或重复，制造假信号，不解决稀疏问题。
只留前 100 token 会丢掉文档后半的相关内容，是信息损失不是缓解。
多召回候选只是把噪声一起捞上来，掩盖不了查询端信号稀疏的根因。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — passages let the query hit the most relevant span, and two encoders fit each side's length, both closing the expression gap.
Padding a 3-word query to thousands injects noise or repetition, faking signal without fixing sparsity.
Keeping only the first 100 tokens drops relevant later content — information loss, not mitigation.
Recalling more candidates just scoops up noise too and cannot mask the root sparse-query signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长文档切成段落分别编码入库，让查询匹配到最相关的那一段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Passage-level indexing splits a long document into separately encoded passages so a query matches the most relevant span.

termDefinitions.term: asymmetric encoder / 非对称编码器
termDefinitions.meaning: 查询和文档用两套不同的编码器，分别适配短查询和长文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An asymmetric encoder uses different encoders for query and document to fit short queries and long docs separately.

q: passage-level indexing 和 asymmetric encoder 各从哪一端解决长度不匹配？
q_en: Which end does passage-level indexing vs an asymmetric encoder fix the mismatch from?
why: passage-level indexing 动的是「文档侧的索引粒度」——把长文档切成段落分别入库；asymmetric encoder 动的是「编码器结构」——查询和文档用两套参数不同的编码器。前者改索引，后者改模型，可叠加。
why_en: Passage-level indexing changes the document-side index granularity by splitting into passages, while an asymmetric encoder changes the encoder architecture with two different encoders — one touches the index, the other the model.
tradeoff: passage-level indexing（改索引粒度）vs asymmetric encoder（改编码器结构）
options: 两者是同一种方法的不同叫法，实现上没有区别
passage 索引改编码器结构，asymmetric encoder 改索引粒度，正好相反
passage 索引改「文档切段的粒度」，asymmetric encoder 改「查询和文档用不同编码器」
两者都只改查询侧，把短查询改写成一段长文本
options_en: They are two names for the same method with no implementation difference.
Passage indexing changes the encoder and the asymmetric encoder changes index granularity — exactly reversed.
Passage indexing changes doc-splitting granularity; the asymmetric encoder gives query and doc different encoders.
Both only change the query side, rewriting the short query into a long passage.
optionExplanations: 不是一回事：一个动索引粒度、一个动编码器结构，落地组件完全不同。
说反了：passage 切的是索引，asymmetric 换的是编码器，别记颠倒。
对；一个从索引侧切段定位、一个从模型侧给长短两端各配编码器，可叠加使用。
两者主要动文档侧和编码器侧，不是把短查询改写成长文本那条路。
optionExplanations_en: Not the same: one changes index granularity, the other the encoder architecture — entirely different components.
Reversed: passage splits the index and asymmetric swaps the encoder; do not flip them.
Correct — one splits and locates on the index side, the other pairs encoders per length on the model side, and they compose.
Both mainly touch the doc side and encoder side, not rewriting the short query into long text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从文档侧动手：切段分别索引，让查询命中最相关段落。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Passage-level indexing acts on the document side: split into passages so the query hits the most relevant span.

termDefinitions.term: asymmetric encoder / 非对称编码器
termDefinitions.meaning: 从模型侧动手：查询和文档各用一套编码器适配长度差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An asymmetric encoder acts on the model side: separate encoders for query and doc to fit the length gap.

scenario_en: You need an offline north-star ranking-quality metric for semantic search, one that requires human-labeled relevance grades.
q: NDCG@k 全称是什么、测什么、下游用来干什么？
q_en: What does NDCG@k stand for, what does it measure, and what does it feed downstream?
why: NDCG@k = Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at k = 归一化折损累计增益，取值 0–1，衡量 top-k 结果的排序质量（相关且排在前面得分高）。它是离线北极星，用来在放量前比较模型排序好坏；代价是需要昂贵的人工相关性标注。
why_en: NDCG@k (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at k) scores top-k ranking quality from 0 to 1 and is the offline north-star for comparing models before rollout, at the cost of expensive human relevance labels.
options: NDCG@k = 每秒查询数，单位 QPS，用来给 ANN 副本做容量规划
NDCG@k = 返回空结果的查询占比，是发现词表覆盖缺口的在线指标
NDCG@k = 有至少一次点击的曝光占比，是衡量结果页质量的在线指标
NDCG@k = 归一化折损累计增益，0–1 分衡量 top-k 排序质量，是离线北极星
options_en: NDCG@k = queries per second, in QPS, used for capacity planning of ANN replicas.
NDCG@k = fraction of queries returning empty, an online metric for vocabulary coverage gaps.
NDCG@k = fraction of impressions with at least one click, an online page-quality metric.
NDCG@k = Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain, a 0-1 score of top-k ranking quality, the offline north-star.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a 0-1 score rewarding relevant results ranked high, measuring top-k ranking quality.

scenario: Amazon 上用户搜一个商品，系统返回空——没有任何结果。这类查询正在悄悄流失销售。
scenario_en: On Amazon a user's product search returns nothing — an empty page silently losing a sale.
q: 哪个指标专门抓「返回空结果」这类失败？
q_en: Which metric specifically catches the 'empty results' failure?
why: Zero-result rate（零结果率）= 返回空结果的查询占比，是在线指标，专抓词表/覆盖缺口——用户想买的东西你根本没召回到，等于丢单。局限是它只看「有没有结果」，不看非空结果的质量。
why_en: Zero-result rate is the fraction of queries returning nothing, an online metric catching vocabulary/coverage gaps — a wanted item never recalled is a lost sale — but it ignores the quality of non-empty results.
tradeoff: 零结果率（抓覆盖缺口/丢单）vs NDCG/click-sat（抓非空结果的排序与质量）
whenOtherWins: 如果结果非空但排得差、点了不满意，零结果率看不出来，得靠 NDCG（排序）或 click satisfaction（点击质量）。
options: NDCG@k：它能直接统计有多少查询返回了空页
SERP CTR：只要出现空结果它就会立刻掉到 0
zero-result rate：返回空结果的查询占比，专抓词表/覆盖缺口导致的丢单
click satisfaction：用停留时长加权，天然覆盖空结果场景
options_en: NDCG@k: it directly counts how many queries returned an empty page.
SERP CTR: it instantly drops to 0 whenever an empty result appears.
Zero-result rate: fraction of queries returning empty, catching coverage-gap lost sales.
Click satisfaction: dwell-weighted, it naturally covers the empty-result case.
optionExplanations: NDCG 测的是非空结果的排序好坏，它需要有结果才能打分，抓不了「压根没结果」。
SERP CTR 是有点击的曝光占比，空结果只是它下降的一个原因，不是专抓覆盖缺口的指标。
对；零结果率直接数「返回空」的查询占比，正好对应词表没覆盖、召回不到的丢单场景。
click satisfaction 衡量点击后的停留质量，空结果连点都没得点，覆盖不到这个失败面。
optionExplanations_en: NDCG scores the ranking of non-empty results and needs results to score, so it cannot catch 'no results at all'.
SERP CTR is the click-bearing impression share; empty results are just one cause of its drop, not a coverage-gap metric.
Correct — zero-result rate counts empty-return queries directly, matching the coverage-gap lost-sale case.
Click satisfaction measures post-click dwell, but an empty result has nothing to click, so it cannot cover this failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回空结果的查询占比，在线指标，抓词表/覆盖缺口导致的丢单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zero-result rate is the fraction of queries returning nothing, an online metric catching coverage-gap lost sales.

scenario: 用户点了某个结果，2 秒就退回来继续找——点了但没真正满足。
scenario_en: A user clicks a result, bounces back in 2 seconds, and keeps searching — a click without satisfaction.
q: click satisfaction（停留加权 CTR）比纯 CTR 多抓住了什么？
q_en: What does click satisfaction (dwell-weighted CTR) catch that raw CTR misses?
why: click satisfaction 用停留时长（dwell time）给点击加权，抓住「点了却秒退」的假点击——结果标题诱人、内容不相关。纯 CTR 只数点没点，会把这种诱导点击也算成功。局限：对 UI 改动敏感。
why_en: Click satisfaction weights clicks by dwell time, catching 'clicked but bounced' fake clicks from tempting-but-irrelevant results, which raw CTR counts as success; its weakness is sensitivity to UI changes.
tradeoff: 停留加权 CTR（抓点后不满意）vs 纯 CTR（只数点击、被诱导点击骗）
options: 它统计返回空结果的比例，比纯 CTR 更早发现覆盖缺口
它用停留时长给点击加权，抓住「点了却秒退」的不相关结果
它只看结果的排序位置，完全不看用户点击后停留多久
它衡量 ANN 的召回延迟，把加载慢的查询算作不满意
options_en: It counts the empty-result share, spotting coverage gaps earlier than raw CTR.
It weights clicks by dwell time, catching 'clicked then bounced' irrelevant results.
It looks only at ranking position and ignores how long users stay after clicking.
It measures ANN recall latency, counting slow-loading queries as dissatisfaction.
optionExplanations: 那是零结果率的活；click satisfaction 看的是点击后的停留质量，不是有没有结果。
对；秒退说明结果不相关，dwell 加权把这种「诱导点击」从成功里剔掉，纯 CTR 做不到。
恰恰相反，它的核心就是点击后停留多久；只看位置的是排序类指标。
延迟是服务侧指标；click satisfaction 衡量的是相关性带来的参与质量，不是速度。
optionExplanations_en: That is zero-result rate's job; click satisfaction watches post-click dwell quality, not whether results exist.
Correct — a fast bounce signals irrelevance, and dwell weighting strips such bait clicks from success, which raw CTR cannot.
Opposite — its core is how long users stay after clicking; position-only is a ranking metric.
Latency is a serving metric; click satisfaction measures engagement quality from relevance, not speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用停留时长加权的 CTR，抓「点了却秒退」的不相关点击。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Click satisfaction is dwell-weighted CTR, catching clicks that bounce fast on irrelevant results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点击后在目标页停留的时间，越长通常越满意。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is how long a user stays on the clicked page; longer usually means more satisfied.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：一次曝光被点击的比例；纯 CTR 不看点后停留质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of impressions clicked; raw CTR ignores post-click dwell quality.

scenario: 结果页展示给用户后，你想知道整页作为一个整体的质量如何。
scenario_en: After a results page is shown, you want to gauge the whole page's quality as a unit.
q: SERP CTR 测什么？它会被什么系统性抬高？
q_en: What does SERP CTR measure, and what systematically inflates it?
why: SERP CTR = 至少产生一次点击的曝光占比，衡量整页质量。它会被导航型查询系统性抬高——「LinkedIn login」几乎必点，把 CTR 撑高，掩盖信息型查询的页面质量问题。
why_en: SERP CTR is the fraction of impressions with at least one click, a whole-page quality signal, and it is systematically inflated by navigational queries like 'LinkedIn login' that almost always get clicked, masking weak informational pages.
options: 至少一次点击的曝光占比，衡量整页质量；被导航型查询系统性抬高
每个结果的平均排序位置，会被很长的查询系统性拉低
返回空结果的查询数量，会被高频热门查询系统性抬高

q: 为什么离线指标达标还不够，要同时上在线指标？

why: 离线 NDCG 只能证明「在标注集上排序更好」，测不出真实用户是否更满意、是否有更多空结果或诱导点击；要同时提在线指标（SERP CTR、click satisfaction）验证真实业务影响。offline 单独不充分。
why_en: Offline NDCG only proves better ranking on a labeled set, not whether real users are more satisfied, so you pair it with online SERP CTR and click satisfaction to verify true business impact.
tradeoff: 只看离线 NDCG（快但不代表真实用户）vs 离线+在线（NDCG 筛质量、在线验业务影响）
whenOtherWins: 如果还在早期迭代、没有线上流量可分，只能先用离线 NDCG 快速筛掉明显差的模型，等有流量再上在线关。

q: 哪个指标最能抓住这种「有结果却没人点」的失败？
q_en: Which metric best catches this 'results exist but nobody clicks' failure?
why: 结果非空所以零结果率正常、看不出问题；用户不点所以 click satisfaction 也没数据；SERP CTR（有点击的曝光占比）会明显下降，专抓「结果在但整页没人点」的页面级失败。
why_en: Since results are non-empty, zero-result rate looks fine; since nobody clicks, click satisfaction has no data; SERP CTR drops clearly, catching the page-level failure of results present but unclicked.
tradeoff: SERP CTR（抓有结果却不点）vs 零结果率（抓没结果）vs click-sat（抓点了不满意）
whenOtherWins: 如果失败是「压根没结果」，那零结果率更直接；如果是「点了但秒退」，那 click satisfaction 更合适——SERP CTR 抓的是「有结果却不点」。

NDCG 是离线标注指标，反映不了线上真实用户点不点的行为。
对；页面有结果但整页没点击，SERP CTR 直接下滑，正是它专抓的页面级失败。
用户根本不点，click satisfaction 就没有点击可加权，这个失败它采不到样。
optionExplanations_en: With non-empty results, zero-result rate reads normal; it only tracks 'are there results', not 'results but no clicks'.
NDCG is an offline labeled metric and cannot reflect real users' online clicking behavior.
Correct — results present but the page unclicked makes SERP CTR fall, exactly the page-level failure it catches.

q: NDCG@k 和 SERP CTR 在「离线/在线」和「测什么」上怎么分工？

why: NDCG@k 是离线指标，用人工标注测排序质量，放量前就能算；SERP CTR 是在线指标，用真实点击测整页质量，只有上了流量才有。一个在实验室、一个在真实用户，互补不能互相替代。
why_en: NDCG@k is offline, measuring ranking quality on human labels before rollout; SERP CTR is online, measuring whole-page quality from real clicks after rollout — complementary, not interchangeable.
tradeoff: NDCG（离线、标注、排序质量）vs SERP CTR（在线、真实点击、整页质量）

q: 这个语料规模直接逼出什么架构决定？

why: 规模是给定事实（Google 数千亿、Amazon 数亿、LinkedIn ~10 亿）——它的下游含义是：在十亿级向量上做精确最近邻要线性扫全库，延迟根本扛不住，所以必须换成 ANN（近似最近邻），牺牲一点召回换亚秒级检索。

q: 该用什么检索结构，代价是什么？
q_en: What retrieval structure should you use, and at what cost?
why: 用 ANN（近似最近邻，如 HNSW、ScaNN）：它用图或量化结构避开全库线性扫描，在十亿级拿到亚秒延迟，代价是牺牲一点召回率（可能漏掉极少数真正最近的向量）。这是延迟换召回的经典取舍。

whenOtherWins: 如果语料很小（几万到几十万向量）、延迟宽松，精确最近邻召回 100% 更省心，不必引入 ANN 的近似误差和索引维护。

继续用精确最近邻，堆更多 CPU 把全库线性扫描并行到亚秒

放弃向量检索退回关键词倒排，这样规模问题就直接消失了

q: HNSW 和 ScaNN 的共同点是什么？

why: 两者都是 ANN 索引算法——HNSW 用分层可导航小世界图、ScaNN 用向量量化+剪枝——目标一致：在十亿级向量上避开精确全扫，用亚秒延迟拿到近似最近邻。它们是同一取舍下的不同实现路线。
why_en: Both are ANN index algorithms — HNSW via a layered navigable small-world graph, ScaNN via vector quantization and pruning — with the same goal of sub-second approximate nearest neighbors at billion scale.
options: 两者都保证返回 100% 精确的最近邻，完全没有召回损失
两者都是关键词倒排索引，和稠密向量检索没有关系
两者都是召回后的排序模型，用来给候选做精排打分

Both are keyword inverted indexes, unrelated to dense vector retrieval.
Both are post-recall ranking models that score candidates for re-ranking.
Both are ANN indexes using graph or quantization to skip the full scan for sub-second approximate neighbors.

它们是召回阶段的索引结构，不是排序模型；精排是下游 re-ranker 的事。
对；HNSW 走图、ScaNN 走量化，路线不同但都为十亿级亚秒近似召回服务。

They index dense vectors and recall by similarity, not keyword inverted lists.

Correct — HNSW is graph-based, ScaNN quantization-based; different routes, both serving billion-scale sub-second approximate recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的 ANN 库，用向量量化+剪枝加速相似检索。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把向量压成有限码字近似表示，减少比较成本，加速 ANN。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vector quantization compresses vectors into a finite codebook approximation, cutting comparison cost to speed ANN.

scenario_en: End-to-end search latency has a sub-200ms SLO to split across query understanding, retrieval, ranking, and rendering.
q: sub-200ms 预算怎么分给四个阶段？它是公式推出来的吗？
q_en: How is the sub-200ms budget split across four stages, and is it derived by formula?
why: sub-200ms 是给定的 SLO（服务级目标），不是公式算出来的——它是产品/体验定的红线。粗分：查询理解 10–30ms、检索(ANN) 50–100ms（最大、最易漂移）、排序 30–60ms、渲染 20–40ms。这个预算约束了每个阶段能用多重的模型。
why_en: The sub-200ms budget is a given SLO, not a derived number, split roughly as query understanding 10-30ms, retrieval 50-100ms, ranking 30-60ms, rendering 20-40ms, and it caps how heavy each stage's model can be.

scenario: 延迟预算里，检索（ANN over dense embeddings）分到 50–100ms，是四个阶段里最大的一块。
scenario_en: In the latency budget, retrieval (ANN over dense embeddings) gets 50-100ms, the largest of the four stages.
q: 为什么检索阶段既是最大延迟块、又最容易出漂移？
q_en: Why is retrieval both the largest latency chunk and the most drift-prone stage?
why: 检索要在十亿级向量上做 ANN 召回，天生是四阶段里最重的一块（50–100ms）；同时它依赖 query encoder 和 doc 向量在同一空间，一旦重训编码器就会 embedding drift，两端不兼容、召回退化。所以它既吃延迟又吃漂移风险。
why_en: Retrieval runs ANN over billions of vectors, inherently the heaviest stage (50-100ms), and depends on query and doc vectors sharing one space, so retraining the encoder causes embedding drift and degraded recall — carrying both latency and drift risk.
options: 因为渲染要等检索返回，检索只是被动背锅，本身既不慢也不会漂移
它在十亿级向量上做 ANN 天生最重；又依赖查询和文档同空间，重训编码器就漂移
因为检索阶段跑的是最贵的 cross-encoder 精排模型，所以才最慢
因为检索每次都要重新训练模型，训练时间被算进了这 50–100ms
options_en: Because rendering waits on retrieval, retrieval is just a passive scapegoat and is neither slow nor drift-prone.
ANN over billions is inherently heaviest, and it depends on query/doc sharing one space, so retraining the encoder drifts it.
Because retrieval runs the most expensive cross-encoder re-ranking model, which is why it is slowest.
Because retrieval retrains a model each time, and the training time is counted in this 50-100ms.
optionExplanations: 检索不是背锅：在十亿向量上做 ANN 本身就最重，且编码器漂移直接砸在它头上。
对；规模让它最耗时，同空间依赖让它对 embedding drift 最敏感，两个风险叠在一个阶段。
cross-encoder 是排序阶段的事，不在检索里；检索用的是双塔向量召回。
检索是在线召回，不含训练；重训是离线的事，不占这 50–100ms 的服务延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Retrieval is no scapegoat: ANN over billions is inherently heaviest, and encoder drift lands squarely on it.
Correct — scale makes it slowest, and shared-space dependence makes it most drift-sensitive; both risks stack on one stage.
The cross-encoder is the ranking stage, not retrieval; retrieval uses two-tower vector recall.
Retrieval is online recall with no training; retraining is offline and does not occupy this 50-100ms serving latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重训查询编码器后新向量与旧文档向量落到不同区域、不兼容，召回退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift: after retraining the query encoder, new vectors land in a different region than old doc vectors, becoming incompatible and degrading recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档编码成同一空间的稠密向量，按相似度召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dense embeddings encode query and doc into one space of dense vectors, recalled by similarity.

scenario: 一个新排序模型 NDCG 更高，但排序阶段多花 +50ms，会把端到端顶破 sub-200ms 的 SLO。
scenario_en: A new ranking model has higher NDCG but adds +50ms to ranking, breaching the end-to-end sub-200ms SLO.
q: 排序更准但要 +50ms，生产评审该怎么判？
q_en: More accurate ranking but +50ms — how should the prod review rule?
why: SLO 是硬红线：NDCG 再高，只要 +50ms 顶破 sub-200ms，端到端就违约，生产评审会拒。质量和延迟是显式取舍——要么把这 50ms 从别处省回来（更快召回/剪枝），要么压缩模型，否则不上。
why_en: The SLO is a hard line: however high NDCG, +50ms breaching sub-200ms violates end-to-end latency and prod review rejects it, forcing you to reclaim the 50ms elsewhere or compress the model.
tradeoff: 更高 NDCG（排序更准）vs sub-200ms SLO（延迟红线，超了就拒）
whenOtherWins: 如果这 50ms 能在别的阶段省回来（如渲染优化、召回剪枝），端到端仍在 200ms 内，那更高 NDCG 的模型就能上。
options: 直接上线：NDCG 是北极星，排序质量优先，延迟超一点无所谓
直接上线：sub-200ms 只是建议值，生产不会真因为延迟拒模型
把 SLO 从 200ms 直接放宽到 250ms 来迁就模型，是最省事的正解
拒或改：SLO 是硬红线，要么从别处省回 50ms，要么压缩模型，否则不上
options_en: Ship it: NDCG is the north-star, ranking quality wins, and a little latency overage is fine.
Ship it: sub-200ms is just advisory, and prod will not really reject a model over latency.
Just loosen the SLO from 200ms to 250ms to accommodate the model — the easiest right answer.
Reject or revise: the SLO is hard — reclaim the 50ms elsewhere or compress the model, else no ship.
optionExplanations: NDCG 高但顶破 SLO，用户等更久、体验崩，生产评审不会为一点排序质量放行。
sub-200ms 是硬 SLO 不是建议；真实评审会因为顶破延迟预算直接拒。
随手放宽 SLO 是把体验红线让给模型，除非有产品依据，否则不能这么迁就。
对；先想办法把 50ms 从召回/渲染省回来或压缩模型，省不回来就不上，延迟是硬约束。
optionExplanations_en: High NDCG that breaches the SLO makes users wait longer and wrecks UX; prod review will not pass it for a little ranking gain.
sub-200ms is a hard SLO, not advice; a real review rejects a model that breaches the latency budget.
Casually loosening the SLO hands the UX line to the model; without product justification you cannot accommodate it this way.
Correct — first reclaim the 50ms from recall/rendering or compress the model; if you cannot, do not ship — latency is a hard constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标：给定的性能红线（sub-200ms），超了就拒，不是可推导数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given performance line (sub-200ms) that rejects on breach, not a derivable number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线排序质量指标，0–1 分；再高也不能违反延迟 SLO。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is an offline 0-1 ranking metric; however high, it cannot violate the latency SLO.

scenario: 你重训了 query encoder，新查询向量落在和旧文档向量不同的语义区域——文档索引还是旧模型编码的。
scenario_en: You retrained the query encoder; new query vectors land in a different region than the doc vectors, which were indexed by the old model.
q: embedding drift 的完整机制和后果是什么？
q_en: What is the full mechanism and consequence of embedding drift?
why: 正常路径：查询和文档向量在同一空间比相似度→重训 query encoder→新查询向量落到不同区域→与旧文档向量语义不兼容→召回退化。恢复动作：re-embed 整个语料（用新模型重编所有文档），代价是网页级要几天+大量算力；retrieval-specific 模型能减轻但消不掉漂移。
why_en: Normally query and doc vectors compare in one space, but retraining the query encoder moves new query vectors to an incompatible region and recall degrades; the fix is re-embedding the whole corpus at a cost of days and heavy compute.
diagram:
flowchart LR E["重训 query encoder"] --> N["新查询向量
落到不同区域"] N --> M["与旧文档向量
语义不兼容"] M --> G["召回退化"] G --> R["re-embed 整个语料
代价:数天+大算力"]
options: 重训查询编码器→新查询向量落到不同区域→与旧文档向量不兼容→召回退化，需 re-embed 全库
重训只会让查询向量更准，文档向量会自动跟着一起更新，不存在不兼容
drift 只是让检索延迟变高，召回结果本身不受影响，加机器即可解决
drift 指索引磁盘碎片化，做一次 compaction 压缩就能恢复
options_en: Retrain query encoder -> new query vectors in a different region -> incompatible with old doc vectors -> recall degrades, needing full re-embed.
Retraining only makes query vectors more accurate, and doc vectors auto-update along with them, so no incompatibility arises.
Drift merely raises retrieval latency; the recall results themselves are unaffected, and adding machines fixes it.
Drift means index disk fragmentation, recoverable with a single compaction pass.
optionExplanations: 对；查询侧换了模型、文档侧没换，两端不在同一空间，召回退化，只能重编全库文档对齐。
文档向量不会自动更新——它们是旧模型编码后固化在索引里的，这正是不兼容的根源。
drift 砸的是召回质量不是延迟：向量对不齐，加机器也召回错的东西。
这不是磁盘碎片；是查询和文档向量语义空间错位，compaction 完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the query side changed models but the doc side did not, so they leave the shared space and recall degrades, fixable only by re-embedding the corpus.
Doc vectors do not auto-update — they are frozen in the index from the old model, which is the very source of incompatibility.
Drift hits recall quality, not latency: with vectors misaligned, more machines just recall the wrong things.
This is not disk fragmentation; it is a semantic-space mismatch between query and doc vectors, and compaction is irrelevant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重训查询编码器后新旧向量落到不同区域、语义不兼容，召回退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift: after retraining the query encoder, new and old vectors land in different, incompatible regions and recall degrades.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询编码成向量的模型；换了它就与旧文档向量不在同一空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query encoder maps a query to a vector; swapping it leaves it out of the old doc vectors' space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型把整个语料的文档重新编码，让两端回到同一空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-embedding re-encodes the entire corpus with the new model so query and doc share one space again.

termDefinitions.term: retrieval-specific model / 检索专用模型
termDefinitions.meaning: 专为检索稳定性训练的编码器，能减轻但不能消除漂移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retrieval-specific model is an encoder trained for retrieval stability, reducing but not eliminating drift.

scenario: query encoder 升级后出现 embedding drift，旧文档向量和新查询向量对不齐，召回在退化。
scenario_en: After a query-encoder upgrade, embedding drift misaligns old doc vectors with new query vectors and retrieval is degrading.
q: 最彻底的缓解手段是什么，代价是什么？
q_en: What is the most thorough mitigation, and at what cost?
why: 最彻底是 re-embed 整个语料——用新编码器把所有文档重编一遍，让两端回到同一空间；代价是网页级几天+巨额算力。用 retrieval-specific 模型（专为检索稳定训练）能减轻漂移，但不能消除，仍需定期重编。
why_en: The most thorough fix is re-embedding the whole corpus with the new encoder to realign both sides, at a cost of days and heavy compute at web scale, while retrieval-specific models reduce but do not eliminate drift.
tradeoff: 全量 re-embed（彻底对齐、几天+大算力）vs retrieval-specific 模型（减轻不消除、省算力）
whenOtherWins: 如果语料小、重编便宜，或漂移轻微、召回退化在容忍范围内，可以先靠 retrieval-specific 模型顶着、延后全量重编，省算力。
options: 回滚到旧的 query encoder，永远不升级模型，drift 就永远不会发生
只重编最近更新过的文档，其余旧向量放着不管也能对齐
re-embed 整个语料，用新编码器重编所有文档回到同空间，代价是几天+大算力
给 ANN 索引加更多副本，用横向扩容来抵消 drift 带来的召回退化
options_en: Roll back to the old query encoder and never upgrade, so drift never happens.
Re-embed only recently updated docs and leave the rest of the old vectors alone — still aligned.
Re-embed the whole corpus with the new encoder back into one space, at a cost of days and heavy compute.
Add more ANN replicas and use horizontal scaling to offset drift's recall degradation.
optionExplanations: 永不升级等于放弃模型改进，drift 是升级的副作用，不能靠冻结模型来假装解决。
只重编部分文档，剩下的旧向量仍和新查询不兼容，语义错位没修好。
对；全量重编让文档和查询回到同一空间，是最彻底的解，代价是网页级几天和大量算力。
加副本只提吞吐/可用性，向量对不齐加多少副本都召回错的，扩容治不了 drift。
optionExplanations_en: Never upgrading forsakes model improvement; drift is a side effect of upgrading, not solved by freezing the model.
Re-embedding only some docs leaves the rest's old vectors incompatible with new queries — the mismatch stays.
Correct — full re-embedding returns docs and queries to one space, the most thorough fix, at a cost of web-scale days and heavy compute.
Replicas only raise throughput/availability; with vectors misaligned, any number of replicas recalls the wrong things — scaling cannot cure drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型重编整个语料的文档，是消除漂移最彻底的手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-embedding re-encodes the whole corpus with the new model, the most thorough way to eliminate drift.

termDefinitions.term: retrieval-specific model / 检索专用模型
termDefinitions.meaning: 为检索稳定性训练的编码器，减轻漂移但不能消除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retrieval-specific model is trained for retrieval stability, reducing but not eliminating drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编码器升级后新旧向量不在同一空间，召回退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift is when an encoder upgrade leaves new and old vectors out of one space, degrading recall.

scenario: 搜索要扛数万 QPS 的在线流量，单个 ANN 实例扛不住。
scenario_en: Search must handle tens of thousands of QPS, more than one ANN instance can serve.
q: 数万 QPS 的吞吐要求逼出哪些系统设计？
q_en: What system designs does tens-of-thousands QPS force?
why: 数万 QPS（每秒查询数）单实例扛不住，要横向扩 ANN 副本（同一索引多副本分摊查询）、前面加负载均衡分流、并做 failover 保证单副本挂了不影响可用性。吞吐是给定量级，决定副本数和容错设计。
why_en: Tens of thousands of QPS overwhelm one instance, so you horizontally scale ANN replicas sharing the query load, put load balancing in front, and add failover so a dead replica does not break availability.
options: 把 ANN 索引压进单机内存，靠垂直扩容一台大机器扛住全部 QPS
横向扩 ANN 副本分摊查询，前置负载均衡分流，做 failover 保可用
给每个查询排队串行处理，用队列削峰就能扛住数万 QPS
提高单次查询的 top-k，让每次多返回结果来减少查询次数
options_en: Cram the ANN index into one machine's memory and vertically scale a single big box to serve all QPS.
Horizontally scale ANN replicas to share load, front them with load balancing, and add failover for availability.
Queue and serially process each query — peak-shaving with a queue handles tens of thousands of QPS.
Raise each query's top-k to return more results and thereby reduce the number of queries.
optionExplanations: 垂直扩一台机器有物理上限，数万 QPS 单机内存和 CPU 都顶不住，必须横向扩副本。
对；多副本分摊 QPS、负载均衡分流、failover 兜底，是高吞吐检索的标准三件套。
串行排队会把延迟拉爆，顶破 sub-200ms SLO；削峰不等于能扛住持续的高吞吐。
加大 top-k 不减少查询次数，反而让每次更重，和吞吐问题南辕北辙。
optionExplanations_en: Vertical scaling on one box hits a physical ceiling; tens of thousands of QPS exceed single-box memory and CPU, so replicate horizontally.
Correct — replicas sharing QPS, load balancing, and failover are the standard trio for high-throughput retrieval.
Serial queuing blows latency past the sub-200ms SLO; peak-shaving does not equal sustaining high throughput.
Raising top-k does not cut query count and makes each query heavier — the opposite of what throughput needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量在线吞吐；数万 QPS 决定副本数和容错设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures online throughput; tens of thousands of QPS set replica count and fault-tolerance design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加更多同构副本分摊负载，而非把单机做大（垂直扩容）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling adds more identical replicas to share load, rather than enlarging one machine (vertical scaling).

termDefinitions.meaning: 某副本挂掉时把流量切到健康副本，保住可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover reroutes traffic to healthy replicas when one dies, preserving availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询在多副本间分流，避免单副本过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load balancing spreads queries across replicas to avoid overloading any one.

scenario: L5 要讲清召回和精排为什么用不同的编码器结构。
scenario_en: At L5 you must explain why recall and re-ranking use different encoder structures.
q: dual-encoder 召回和 cross-encoder 精排差在哪一维？
q_en: On what dimension do a dual-encoder for recall and a cross-encoder for re-ranking differ?
why: dual-encoder（双塔）分别编码查询和文档，可离线预算文档向量、在线只算查询向量做 ANN，快但精度低；cross-encoder 把查询和文档拼在一起联合编码，能建模细粒度交互、精度高，但每对都要在线算、贵，只能用在召回后的少量候选上精排。
why_en: A dual-encoder encodes query and doc separately so doc vectors precompute offline and only the query is encoded online for ANN — fast but less precise — while a cross-encoder co-encodes the pair for fine-grained interaction, precise but expensive, so it only re-ranks a few candidates.
tradeoff: dual-encoder（快、可预算、精度低）vs cross-encoder（精度高、贵、只精排少量）
options: dual-encoder 分开编码、可离线预算、快，用于大规模召回；cross-encoder 联合编码、精度高但贵，只做精排
两者网络结构完全相同，唯一区别是 dual 跑在 GPU、cross 跑在 CPU 上
cross-encoder 因为更快所以拿来做大规模召回，dual-encoder 更准所以放在精排
两者都能把全部文档向量离线预算好，在线的计算开销其实完全一样
options_en: Dual-encoder encodes separately, precomputes offline, and is fast for large-scale recall; cross-encoder co-encodes, is precise but costly, and only re-ranks.
Their networks are identical; the only difference is dual runs on GPU and cross runs on CPU.
Cross-encoder is faster so it does large-scale recall, and dual-encoder is more accurate so it does re-ranking.
Both can precompute all doc vectors offline, and their online compute cost is actually identical.
optionExplanations: 对；双塔查询文档各编各的、文档向量可离线存好，在线快；cross 拼一起算交互更准但每对都算，只精排。
结构本质不同：dual 是两座独立塔、cross 是单塔联合编码，不是 GPU/CPU 的区别。
说反了：cross 慢而准用于精排，dual 快而糙用于召回，别记颠倒。
只有 dual 能离线预算文档向量；cross 必须查询到达后才能和文档联合编码，在线开销大得多。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — two towers encode query and doc separately with doc vectors stored offline for fast online recall; cross co-encodes for precision but scores every pair, so only re-ranking.
The architectures differ fundamentally: dual is two separate towers, cross is one joint encoder — not a GPU/CPU distinction.
Reversed: cross is slow-but-precise for re-ranking, dual is fast-but-coarse for recall — do not flip them.
Only dual can precompute doc vectors offline; cross must co-encode with the doc after the query arrives, far costlier online.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询和文档分别编码成向量，文档向量可离线预算，用于大规模召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual-encoder (two-tower) encodes query and doc into separate vectors, precomputing doc vectors offline for large-scale recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档拼在一起联合编码，建模细粒度交互，精度高但只能精排少量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder co-encodes query and doc together for fine-grained interaction, precise but only for re-ranking a few candidates.

scenario: 同一道语义搜索题，L4、L5、Staff+ 候选人被期待答出的深度不同。
scenario_en: For the same semantic-search question, L4, L5, and Staff+ candidates are expected to answer at different depths.
q: 什么最能把 Staff+ 的答法和 L4/L5 区分开？
q_en: What most distinguishes a Staff+ answer from L4/L5?
why: L4 给出问题定义+基础管道（encoder→ANN→ranker）+核心指标；L5 会拆查询理解、讲 dual vs cross-encoder 取舍、把 drift 当运营风险；Staff+ 主动驱动 framing、分配延迟预算、点出长度不匹配和反馈回路、权衡全量重编 vs 增量更新。越高越主动、越讲 org 级取舍。
why_en: L4 defines the problem, basic pipeline, and core metrics; L5 decomposes query understanding, weighs dual vs cross-encoder, and treats drift as operational risk; Staff+ proactively drives framing, allocates the latency budget, raises length mismatch and feedback loops, and weighs full re-embed vs incremental.
tradeoff: L4（定义+基础管道+核心指标）vs Staff+（主动 framing+延迟预算+反馈回路+org 取舍）
whenOtherWins: 如果是 L4 面试，能清晰给出基础管道和核心指标就达标，不必主动扛延迟预算分配和 org 级取舍——那是 Staff+ 的加分项。
options: Staff+ 要背出更多模型名字和论文，比 L4 记得多就够了
Staff+ 只要把 ANN 底层图结构讲得比 L4 更细就算到位
Staff+ 主动驱动 framing、分配延迟预算、点出长度不匹配和反馈回路、权衡重编 vs 增量
Staff+ 和 L4 答法一样，只是 Staff+ 要多写一些伪代码
options_en: Staff+ just needs to recite more model names and papers than L4.
Staff+ only needs to explain ANN's graph internals in more detail than L4.
Staff+ proactively drives framing, allocates the latency budget, raises length mismatch and feedback loops, and weighs re-embed vs incremental.
Staff+ answers the same as L4, only writing a bit more pseudocode.
optionExplanations: 区分不在记多少模型名，而在能否主动 framing、扛下延迟预算和 org 级取舍。
讲细 ANN 图结构是实现深度，不是 Staff+ 信号；Staff+ 看的是系统级主动权。
对；主动驱动 framing、分延迟预算、点反馈回路和重编 vs 增量取舍，是 Staff+ 的判别特征。
写伪代码不是分级依据；层级差在系统思维的主动性和取舍深度。
optionExplanations_en: The distinction is not how many model names you recall but whether you drive framing and own latency-budget and org-level tradeoffs.
Detailing ANN graph internals is implementation depth, not a Staff+ signal; Staff+ is judged on system-level initiative.
Correct — proactively driving framing, allocating the latency budget, and weighing feedback loops and re-embed vs incremental is the Staff+ marker.
Pseudocode volume is not the leveling criterion; the gap is initiative and depth of tradeoff in systems thinking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工程职级：L4 定义问题+基础管道，L5 拆解取舍，Staff+ 主动驱动 framing 和 org 级取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L4/L5/Staff+ are engineering levels: L4 defines problem and pipeline, L5 decomposes tradeoffs, Staff+ drives framing and org-level tradeoffs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编码器升级后向量不兼容、召回退化，L5 起要当运营风险讨论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift is post-upgrade vector incompatibility degrading recall, discussed as operational risk from L5 up.

q: 把一次语义搜索请求的四个处理阶段排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the four processing stages of one semantic-search request.
steps: 检索：ANN 在稠密向量上召回候选
查询理解：意图分类+实体识别+消歧
渲染：组装 SERP 结果页返回
排序：cross-encoder / 特征精排候选
why: 请求主线是查询理解→检索→排序→渲染，正好对应 sub-200ms 预算的四段。理解先把查询变成意图/实体，检索用 ANN 拉候选，排序精排，渲染组页返回；顺序错了下游就没有输入。
why_en: A request flows query understanding to retrieval to ranking to rendering, matching the four latency-budget stages, since each stage needs the previous one's output.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["查询理解
意图/实体/消歧"] --> R["检索
ANN 召回候选"] R --> K["排序
精排候选"] K --> D["渲染
组装 SERP"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻，检索阶段在稠密向量上召回候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) recalls candidates over dense vectors in the retrieval stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序阶段把查询和候选联合编码做精排的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder co-encodes query and candidate to re-rank in the ranking stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 渲染阶段组装并返回给用户的结果页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SERP (Search Engine Results Page) is the results page assembled and returned in the rendering stage.

scenario: 语料在持续更新，你要在「模型升级后全量重编」和「只对新增/变更文档增量更新索引」之间做 org 级取舍。
scenario_en: The corpus keeps changing; you must weigh full re-embedding after a model upgrade against incremental index updates for only new/changed docs.
q: 全量重编和增量更新该怎么权衡？
q_en: How do you weigh full re-embedding against incremental updates?
why: 全量 re-embed 保证所有文档和新查询在同一空间、召回最一致，但网页级要几天+巨额算力；增量更新只重编新增/变更文档，便宜快，但换了编码器后新旧向量混在一个索引里会不兼容。取舍轴是「一致性 vs 成本」，换编码器偏全量，仅内容变动偏增量。
why_en: Full re-embedding keeps all docs in one space with the most consistent recall but costs days and huge compute at web scale, while incremental updates only re-embed changed docs cheaply but mix incompatible old and new vectors after an encoder swap — the axis is consistency vs cost.
tradeoff: 全量重编（一致性最好、贵、慢）vs 增量更新（省、快、换编码器后新旧不兼容）
whenOtherWins: 如果只是新增/删除文档、编码器没换，增量更新就够且更省；只有编码器升级导致全库向量不兼容时，才值得付全量重编的代价。
options: 永远只做增量更新，全量重编太贵，任何情况下都不该做
永远做全量重编，一致性最重要，成本完全不用考虑
两者随便选，结果都一样，纯看当天算力有没有空
换编码器导致全库不兼容时全量重编，只是内容增删时增量更新，轴是一致性 vs 成本
options_en: Always do incremental only — full re-embedding is too costly and should never be done.
Always do full re-embedding — consistency is paramount and cost need not be considered.
Pick either freely; results are identical, purely depending on spare compute that day.
Full re-embed when an encoder swap makes the corpus incompatible, incremental for content add/remove — the axis is consistency vs cost.
optionExplanations: 只增量的话，编码器一升级新旧向量就混在一个索引里不兼容，召回退化拦不住。
每次都全量重编，网页级几天+巨额算力，内容只是小改时纯属浪费。
两者结果不一样：一致性和成本差很大，不能凭当天算力随意选。
对；编码器升级要全量对齐、内容增删走增量，取舍轴就是召回一致性 vs 重编成本。
optionExplanations_en: Incremental-only means an encoder upgrade mixes incompatible old and new vectors in one index, and recall degradation cannot be stopped.
Full re-embedding every time costs web-scale days and huge compute — pure waste when only content changed slightly.
The two are not equivalent: consistency and cost differ greatly, so you cannot pick by spare compute.
Correct — an encoder upgrade needs a full realign while content add/remove goes incremental; the axis is recall consistency vs re-embed cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型重编整个语料，一致性最好但代价是几天+大算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-embedding re-encodes the whole corpus with the new model, most consistent but costing days and heavy compute.

termDefinitions.term: incremental index update / 增量索引更新
termDefinitions.meaning: 只对新增/变更文档更新向量，便宜快但换编码器后会新旧混用不兼容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An incremental index update re-embeds only new/changed docs, cheap and fast but mixing incompatible old/new vectors after an encoder swap.

scenario: 用户点击哪些结果会回流成下一轮训练数据，训练出的模型又决定展示哪些结果。
scenario_en: Which results users click feeds back as next-round training data, and the trained model decides what to show next.
q: 点击→重训的反馈回路会带来什么风险？
q_en: What risk does the click-to-retraining feedback loop introduce?
why: 模型决定展示什么→用户只能点被展示的→这些点击回流成训练数据→强化「已被展示」的结果，形成自我强化回路。风险是流行度偏置和位置偏置被放大，长尾/新文档拿不到曝光就永远学不到，短期指标好看但多样性和召回覆盖在退化。Staff+ 要主动点出这条回路。
why_en: The model decides what shows, users can only click what is shown, those clicks feed training and reinforce already-shown results — a self-reinforcing loop that amplifies popularity and position bias, so long-tail and new docs never get exposure to be learned.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["模型决定展示什么"] --> S["用户只能点被展示的"]
  S --> D["点击回流成训练数据"]
  D --> M
options: 没有风险：点击是真实信号，回流训练只会让模型单调地变得更好
风险只是训练变慢，因为数据量会随着点击不断变大
自我强化回路放大流行/位置偏置，长尾文档拿不到曝光就学不到，覆盖退化
回路只影响渲染阶段的 UI 样式，和召回质量、训练数据都无关
options_en: No risk: clicks are real signal, so feeding them back only makes the model monotonically better.
The only risk is slower training, since data volume keeps growing with clicks.
The self-reinforcing loop amplifies popularity/position bias; long-tail docs get no exposure to be learned, and coverage degrades.
The loop only affects rendering-stage UI styling, unrelated to recall quality or training data.
optionExplanations: 点击不是无偏信号——用户只能点被展示的，回流训练会把展示偏置当成真相强化。
数据变大不是核心风险；核心是回路把偏置越滚越大，不是训练时长。
对；被展示的越被点、越被强化，长尾和新文档拿不到曝光就永远学不到，多样性和覆盖退化。
回路直接改训练数据分布和召回覆盖，不只是 UI；这正是它危险的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Clicks are not unbiased — users can only click what is shown, so feeding them back reinforces exposure bias as if it were truth.
Growing data is not the core risk; the core is the loop compounding bias, not training duration.
Correct — shown results get clicked and reinforced, so long-tail and new docs get no exposure to be learned, and diversity and coverage degrade.
The loop directly changes the training-data distribution and recall coverage, not just UI — which is exactly why it is dangerous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的展示决策塑造未来训练数据，自我强化，放大偏置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop is when the model's exposure decisions shape future training data, self-reinforcing and amplifying bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热门结果因常被展示常被点而不断被强化，挤压长尾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity bias is when popular results, shown and clicked often, keep getting reinforced, squeezing out the long tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排在前面的结果因更易被看到而更常被点，与真实相关性混淆。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is when higher-ranked results get more clicks simply for being seen, confounding true relevance.
